intro: If you've been searching for an FUE hair transplant near me, you're probably weighing up where to have it done and who should carry it out, close enough to home for the consultations and any follow-up. FUE moves individual follicles from a donor area to thinning areas under local anaesthetic, and it's worth understanding who will actually be doing the work before you go ahead. iComply can introduce you to a suitable UK cosmetic surgeon in your area who will quote you directly, with the price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an FUE hair transplant nearby usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a local FUE hair transplant want clarity on who will perform the procedure and what a sensible, unhurried route to it looks like.
needs: You want a surgeon close enough to travel to comfortably for the initial consultation and any follow-up appointments.
You're unsure whether the person carrying out the transplant will be the surgeon or technicians, and you want the surgeon involved throughout.
You've read about FUE moving individual follicles under local anaesthetic and want to talk it through properly with someone qualified before deciding.
You want time to reflect on the decision rather than being pushed towards booking by high-pressure sales.
You'd like a clear quote for the work, given as price on application, so you can compare options without being rushed.
context_heading: Who should be carrying out your FUE transplant
context: Cosmetic surgery, including FUE hair transplants, should be carried out by a surgeon on the GMC's specialist register, usually in plastic surgery or a related specialty, in a hospital or clinic registered with the CQC in England (or the equivalent regulator elsewhere in the UK). Your consultation should be with the surgeon who will actually operate, not just a salesperson or technician. The GMC also requires doctors offering cosmetic interventions to give you time to reflect before you agree to surgery, and not to use high-pressure sales tactics.

FUE results take months to appear, so it's worth being patient and realistic about what the procedure can achieve. Asking who will perform each part of the procedure, and where it will take place, helps you judge whether a clinic is right for you.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say where you're based and how far you're willing to travel for an FUE hair transplant near you.
Explain the areas of thinning you're concerned about and whether you've had any hair transplant before.
Mention whether you've already spoken to a surgeon or clinic about FUE, and what you were told.
Note any medical conditions or medications that might affect surgery under local anaesthetic, so the surgeon can consider them.
Say whether you'd prefer the surgeon to be a member of BAAPS or BAPRAS, or to hold the Royal College of Surgeons cosmetic surgery certification.
Make clear you'd like a quote given as price on application, so you know what to expect before committing.
questions: Will you, the surgeon, be carrying out the whole FUE procedure, or will technicians do part of it?
Are you on the GMC's specialist register, and in which specialty?
Is the clinic registered with the CQC, and where will the procedure take place?
How will you decide whether FUE is suitable for my pattern of hair loss?
What should I expect in the months after the procedure, and when will results start to show?
Can you give me a quote as price on application, and explain what it covers?

faqs.a: FUE moves individual follicles from a donor area to thinning areas, and it's performed under local anaesthetic. Your surgeon should explain the procedure and what it can realistically achieve at consultation.

faqs.q: Should the surgeon be involved, or can technicians do it?
faqs.a: Cosmetic surgery should be carried out by a surgeon on the GMC's specialist register, and your consultation should be with the surgeon who will operate. It's reasonable to ask who will perform each part of the procedure.

faqs.q: How long until I see results?
faqs.a: FUE results take months to appear, so it's worth being patient. Your surgeon can explain what to expect over time.
Clinics in England must be registered with the CQC, with equivalent regulators elsewhere in the UK. You can ask the clinic which regulator it is registered with before you go ahead.
